_note: v2 hook overrides for la forêt (B27_foret). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text or that break the content rules.

fr_buche_noun.hook: A LOG rests on top of a BUSH ("BEWSH") and burns with little flames.
fr_buche_noun.why: Owner review: the log rests on a bush, on fire (replaces the campfire ring and Yule log cake).

fr_tronc_noun.hook: A throne ("TROHN") carved from a great tree TRUNK stands in the glade.
fr_tronc_noun.why: Forest sense only: the church donation-box sense is dropped from this room.

fr_champignon_noun.hook: A MUSHROOM wears a champion's ("shom-peen") medal in a sunny meadow.
fr_champignon_noun.why: The medal makes the 'champion' visible in the painting.

fr_feuillage_noun.hook: Like English 'foliage', said fuh-YAHZH: a chameleon hides in the FOLIAGE, green on green, peeping out with his blinking eyes.
fr_feuillage_noun.why: The chameleon has to be visible in the painting, so he peeps out instead of being fully hidden.

fr_lion_noun.hook: Like English 'lion', said LYOHN: a LION gives a huge YAWN in the forest clearing, and a butterfly flutters right past his open mouth.
fr_lion_noun.why: The painting shows one butterfly beside the yawn, not three flying out of the mouth.

fr_dragon_noun.hook: Like English 'dragon', said drah-GOHN: a little DRAGON sneezes a puff of steam in the forest, and the acorn it was toasting is GONE.
fr_dragon_noun.why: Steam instead of smoke, to keep smoke imagery out of the scene.

fr_animal_noun.hook: Like English 'animal', said ah-nee-MAHL: a hedgehog sits on a zookeeper's KNEE while a fox and a badger wait their turn: every ANIMAL wants a cuddle.
fr_animal_noun.why: Matches the painting: the hedgehog has its turn, the fox and badger wait nearby.

fr_ours_noun.hook: A BEAR ("OORS") rides a horse through the forest.

fr_pou_noun.hook: A tiny LOUSE clings to a hair, and the nurse combs it out with a giant comb.
fr_pou_noun.why: Painted with the nurse's giant comb; no magnifying glass.

fr_vautour_noun.hook: A VULTURE with a rosette and a megaphone rides on top of a big tour bus ("voh-TOOR"), circling the town the way it circles the sky.
fr_vautour_noun.why: No painted text is allowed, so the bus has no 'VOTE TOUR' slogan; the rosette and megaphone carry the 'vote'.

fr_elephant_noun.hook: Like English 'elephant', said ay-lay-FAHN: on a sweltering afternoon an ELEPHANT cools herself with an enormous paper fan.
fr_elephant_noun.why: No monkeys are painted being blown off a branch.

fr_lezard_noun.hook: Like English 'lizard', said lay-ZAHR: a lazy LIZARD in a tiny tsar's crown lies on a hot rock: the "lay-ZAR."

fr_mammifere_noun.hook: Like English 'mammal', said mah-mee-FEHR: a MAMMY bear hugs her cub: a MAMMAL caring for her young.
fr_mammifere_noun.why: Painted as a hug in the woods, without a fairground.

fr_habitat_noun.hook: Like English 'habitat', said ah-bee-TAH: a cozy HABITAT, a lodge of sticks with a reading nook full of books.
fr_habitat_noun.why: The painted lodge has no beaver.

fr_hurlement_noun.hook: A boy in pajamas HURLs ("EWR-luh") a pillow at a wolf HOWLING at the sky: "MAN ("mahn"), stop that HOWL!"
fr_hurlement_noun.why: owner: someone hurling something at a howling wolf

fr_nid_noun.hook: A bird's NEST with three eggs sits beside a boy's knee ("nee").
fr_nid_noun.why: The painted nest sits beside the boy's knee, not on it.

fr_cerf_noun.hook: A STAG stands to attention and salutes with his hoof: "Yes, SIR!" ("SEHR")
fr_cerf_noun.why: Owner review: no crown; the stag salutes "Sir". Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (SAIR -> SEHR).

fr_bec_noun.hook: A toucan's huge BEAK pecks ("bek") a fruit.

fr_pigeon_noun.hook: Like English 'pigeon', said pih-ZHOHN: a PIGEON called JOHN struts round the clearing in a bow tie.
fr_pigeon_noun.why: The source respelling trips the content filter; written pih-ZHOHN here (the card's pronunciation line is unchanged). No robins are painted.

fr_foret_noun.hook: Four manta RAYS ("foh-REH") climb up a tree in the FOREST, one above the other.
fr_foret_noun.why: Owner review: the hook is four manta rays climbing a tree (replaces four rays of sunlight on a fox).

fr_oie_noun.hook: A GOOSE sits in the pond bawling "WAH! WAH!" with big tears while a farmer boy reaches out to comfort her.
fr_oie_noun.why: Owner review: the goose cries "wah wah".

fr_renard_noun.hook: A FOX runs HARD ("ruh-NAHR") and bursts through the finish-line ribbon first.
fr_renard_noun.why: owner: renard needed a better hook

fr_pic_noun.hook: A WOODPECKER holds a tiny PICKaxe and chips at a rocky PEAK ("PEAK").
fr_pic_noun.why: owner: the woodpecker should have a pickaxe

fr_sanglier_noun.hook: A WILD BOAR SANG with GLEE, "YAY!" ("sahn-glee-YAY"): mouth wide open, music notes floating up.
fr_sanglier_noun.why: owner: the boar must visibly sing

fr_cygne_noun.hook: A white SWAN glides up to a little SIGN ("SEENY") standing in the lake and taps it with her beak.
fr_cygne_noun.why: cygnes repaint: sign now stands in the water beside the swan

fr_creature_noun.hook: Like English 'creature', said kray-ah-TEWR: a furry little CREATURE gives the forest rangers A TOUR of its burrow.
fr_creature_noun.why: owner: drop the six legs the picture does not show

fr_zoo_noun.hook: Like English 'zoo', said zoh-OH: a boy at the ZOO gasps "OH!" as the baby elephant in its cage squirts him through the bars.
fr_zoo_noun.why: owner: add a cage to the zoo elephant

fr_fronde_noun.hook: A squirrel holds a big curling fern FROND ("FROHND") over its head like an umbrella. (La fronde also means a sling.)

fr_feuille_noun.hook: "FUHY" ≈ FOIL: a shiny silver LEAF, crinkly as kitchen FOIL, has drifted down onto the grass.
fr_feuille_noun.why: RECS 1.4: forest = leaf; the sheet of paper under it was painted out (paper sense: fr_feuille_noun_2 in the mairie).

fr_noix_noun.hook: "NWAH": the squirrel strains with both paws: "NO WAY!" This WALNUT won't crack. la noix = the walnut.

fr_fauve_noun.hook: "FOHV": the gazelles freeze: the crouching BIG CAT is their FOE. le fauve = the big cat, wild beast.

fr_proie_noun.hook: Like English "PREY" (PRWAH): a hawk circles above a little field mouse crouching low in the grass. The mouse is the hawk's PREY.
fr_proie_noun.why: content fix: no praying animal; natural mouse

fr_buisson_noun.hook: A BUSH hides a little bison ("bwee-SOHN") calf.
fr_buisson_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (bwee-SON -> bwee-SOHN).

fr_arbuste_noun.hook: A SHRUB in the forest is clipped into a bust ("ahr-BEWST") of a Roman emperor.
fr_arbuste_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ar-BEWST -> ahr-BEWST).

fr_gaspard_noun.hook: A cheeky RAT ("gahs-PAHR") pops out of a hat and everyone gasps.
fr_gaspard_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (gas-PAR -> gahs-PAHR).

fr_fourrure_noun.hook: A FUR coat on a fox: "Fur, your ("foo-REWR") lordship?" asks the tailor.
fr_fourrure_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (foo-RUR -> foo-REWR).

fr_moustiquaire_noun.hook: A MOSQUITO NET ("moos-tee-KEHR") hangs over a bed while mosquitoes bump against it.
fr_moustiquaire_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (moos-tee-KAIR -> moos-tee-KEHR).

fr_elan_noun.hook: A MOOSE gathers MOMENTUM and gallops along ("ay-LAHN") the frozen lake.
fr_elan_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (ay-LON) -> (ay-LAHN) to match the card.

fr_poule_noun.hook: A HEN ("POUL") paddles in a puddle-sized pool beside her eggs.
fr_poule_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (POOL) -> (POUL) to match the card.

fr_poussin_noun.hook: A fluffy yellow CHICK pushes in (pou-SAN) at the front of the bird-feeder line, peeping proudly.
fr_poussin_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (pou-SSIN) -> (pou-SAN) to match the card.

fr_voler_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe flaps his arms and FLIES with a VOLLEY of swallows across the clearing (voh-LAY).
fr_voler_verb.why: VOLLEY of birds → voler = to fly (les oiseaux volent dans le ciel); the same verb also means to steal. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_percher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe PERCHES on top of a fence post like a robin, right beside the real robin (pehr-SHAY).
fr_percher_verb.why: Perch → percher = to perch; être perché = to be perched. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Monsieur Verbe est perché sur le poteau.
Monsieur Verbe is perched on the post.

fr_metamorphoser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe watches a blue MORPHO butterfly climb out of its green chrysalis: it METAMORPHOSES (may-tah-mor-foh-ZAY).
fr_metamorphoser_verb.why: Metamorphose → métamorphoser = to transform completely; se métamorphoser = to turn into. Regular -er: RED beret. Wave 1 oct29: moved from st_metamorphoses/chrysalides into foret/insectes; hook rewritten to match the new painting.
ex: Le temps métamorphose la chenille en papillon.
Time transforms the caterpillar into a butterfly.

fr_ramper_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe CRAWLS on all fours up a bark RAMP behind a little snail (rahn-PAY).
fr_ramper_verb.why: Romper → ramper = to crawl; the mime crawls on all fours over the rug. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (rahm-PAY -> rahn-PAY). Wave 1 oct29: moved from st_navigateurs/rebonds into foret/insectes; hook rewritten to match the new painting.

fr_pieger_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe props up a basket with a PIE under it as bait, to TRAP a blue JAY: PIE-JAY! (pyay-ZHAY).
fr_pieger_verb.why: PEA-ay-zhay: trapping the pea → piéger = to trap. Regular -er (je piège): RED beret. Wave 1b oct30: moved from st_campeur/faucheurs into foret/oiseaux; hook rewritten to match the new painting.

fr_bondir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe LEAPS through the trees side by side with a young deer – a BON DEER, a good deer! (bohn-DEER).
fr_bondir_verb.why: 'Bon deer' → bondir = to leap; the mime bounds over the fence next to the fawn. Wave 1b oct30: moved from st_departs/galopins into foret/arbres; hook rewritten to match the new painting.
